Q18663552.summary: Within a painted arched frame, a tall, youthful Christ in a white tunic and pallium turns and extends his hand toward a woman who kneels at his feet, wrapped in a dark mantle, reaching out to touch the hem of his garment. The moment of faith and healing is told with great economy: two figures, one gesture, and the compassion of the Lord who said, 'Your faith has made you well.'
facts: This is one of very few surviving catacomb paintings of the healing of the woman with the issue of blood (the haemorrhoissa).
The Catacombs of Marcellinus and Peter on the ancient Via Labicana are among the richest in painted chambers of the late 3rd and 4th centuries.

Q18663552.notes: Sources vary between late 3rd century and early/mid 4th century; Wikidata records 300.

cur:catacombs2-narbonne-continuous-friez.summary: A long, unbroken procession of figures in togas and short tunics fills this fragment, without trees or columns to separate the scenes. At the left a figure sits in a basket-weave chair, the type used for the Virgin receiving the Magi, approached by men in short tunics; towards the right a youthful figure stretches his hand over a basket held out to him, as Christ blesses the loaves, while a veiled woman stands near the centre.
facts: The museum label recorded on Commons notes that it was reused in the walls of the Stadieu house in Narbonne, and that its continuous frieze is unusual for the period.
cur:catacombs2-narbonne-continuous-friez.notes: The scenes are not identified in the sources consulted; the Magi and the multiplication of the loaves are proposed from the composition and are uncertain.
